400.body:
## Summary

This issue is the delivery design for shipping ScienceDiscovery as a **desktop application on Windows and macOS**: one installer, one window, a first-run wizard, and automatic updates — with the code-execution and sandbox story settled per platform.

It is the design-level follow-up to #34 (desktop window) and #31 (Windows support), and it answers the questions those two left open: which shell framework, what to do about a Windows sandbox, how macOS gets a binary plus signing and notarization, and how updates reach installed apps. It also supplies the update mechanism asked for in #32.

## Where the product stands today

| Platform | Current state |
|---|---|
| Linux | Released binary and source mode; the UI is a browser tab on `127.0.0.1:4310`, reached with a bearer token. |
| macOS | Source mode only, officially supported on macOS 13+; sandbox is native (Seatbelt). No binary, no installer, no signing or notarization. |
| Windows | Not supported in any form. The existing `bubblewrap` + seccomp sandbox is Linux-only, and the runner, startup script, and binary packaging all assume a Linux or Darwin host. |

The practical effect: getting to a first screen means a terminal, a token copy-paste, and a browser tab, and a large group of researchers is excluded outright.

## Goals

- Download → install → wizard → working workspace, with no terminal, no token handling, and no manual environment setup.
- Windows covered without WSL being mandatory.
- Code execution stays inside the security contract the project already states, on both platforms.
- One shell codebase, one packaging pipeline, one release pipeline for both platforms.
- Installed apps keep themselves current.

## Non-goals for v1

- No Linux desktop build (Linux stays binary + browser).
- No forked frontend: the shell loads the same `apps/web` build against the same control API.
- No remote-execution provider on macOS. The remote link itself is cross-platform; only the Linux-hosted target ships with v1.
- No multi-instance support. Ports stay fixed and unique.
- No enterprise deployment formats (no Windows MSI, no macOS pkg).

## Root decisions

| Decision | Choice | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| Shell | Electron, shared by both platforms | Same runtime family as the Node backend, identical rendering engine on every platform (the UI leans on Molstar, Plotly, Cytoscape), and the window, token injection, wizard, and orderly shutdown come for free. ~200 MB of memory is the accepted cost. |
| Execution environment | Windows: provider-based, direct execution by default, WSL and remote demoted to optional plugins. macOS: Seatbelt by default, fail-closed if unavailable, no remote. | On Windows the sandbox was always an interchangeable provider, so WSL becomes a plugin rather than the foundation — users who cannot install WSL are not shut out. On macOS the sandbox is already built into the OS and available on probe. |
| Bundling | Layered | Base package ~500–700 MB and works offline; large pieces (the WSL rootfs on Windows, heavy scientific dependencies) ship as on-demand plugin volumes; macOS ships per-architecture packages. |
| Architecture matrix | Windows: x64 only, tiered by OS version. macOS: 13+, arm64 as the mainline plus an x64 build. | Windows arm64 volumes do not justify the work yet, and direct execution has no hard WSL dependency, so older Windows versions remain covered. On macOS the conda scientific stack splits by architecture and a CPython/conda environment cannot be a universal binary. |
| Ordering | Windows is the first target platform, macOS the second. | Sharing the shell, packaging, and release pipeline costs the least when done once; macOS needs no backend adaptation and has a native sandbox, so it can reach internal beta sooner. |

## Execution model

### Shared

SD already models isolation as a replaceable enum — `bubblewrap` on Linux, `seatbelt` on macOS, chosen automatically by the backend. The desktop work adds a second, orthogonal question: **where** code runs.

### Windows: an execution-provider routing layer

- A routing layer above the existing sandbox enum answers "where does code run" with `windows-direct | wsl | remote`. The two layers stay independent: routing to WSL still isolates with bubblewrap inside it; routing to direct execution falls back to the approval mode because Windows has no OS-level sandbox. The existing enum does not change — new code is layered on top, so upstream merges continue to apply.
- **Capability probing, fail-closed.** The router assumes nothing about the machine: at startup it checks whether WSL is present, whether the private sandbox instance has been imported, and whether a remote host is configured. This reuses the existing sandbox-probe mechanism, caches the result for the session, and treats anything indeterminate as unavailable rather than routing on unknown state.
- **Hot switching.** Finishing a plugin install re-probes without restarting the backend. A persistent badge shows the active mode: sandboxed, direct, or remote.
- **Direct execution path.** The `run_shell` tool is bash-syntax and the model depends on it, so the bundled starter environment includes a bash compatibility layer (the MSYS2 port). Without it, direct execution could not run code at all.
- **Provider B (WSL plugin).** A trimmed, purpose-built Linux rootfs (~200 MB: bash, bubblewrap, system libraries, python3) imported under a dedicated instance name via `wsl --import`, bypassing the Store and its 1–2 GB download. Installation is a six-step state machine (detect → platform install → rootfs import → dependency check → network check → payload placement) with a journal after each step so an interrupted install resumes. A redistribution-compliance review of the Ubuntu base is required before this work starts; if it does not clear, the base moves to Debian.
- **No dead ends.** If the plugin cannot be installed, the user keeps direct execution, gets a specific failure reason with illustrated guidance, and has one-click rollback. Uninstalling the plugin deregisters the instance, clears the rootfs, and returns to direct execution with no residue.

### macOS: native sandbox, no routing layer

- macOS is a Unix platform; the backend stack already runs there in source mode, and Seatbelt is built in. The three heaviest pieces of the Windows plan — backend adaptation, the provider routing layer plus WSL plugin system, and the unsandboxed fallback — disappear or shrink sharply here.
- The default tier **is** the full sandbox. There are no plugins to install and no mode to switch; the mode badge stays visible and reads "sandboxed".
- If Seatbelt is unavailable (MDM-managed machines, nested sandboxing), the app fails closed with an explicit error and diagnostics. It does not degrade to unsandboxed execution the way Windows does.

## Packaging, signing, and distribution

| Area | Windows | macOS |
|---|---|---|
| Toolchain | electron-builder — one configuration produces both platform targets | same |
| Installer | NSIS, per-user install under `%LocalAppData%\Programs`, no UAC elevation anywhere | Standard DMG drag to `/Applications`; no permission special-casing |
| Artifact naming | `ScienceDiscovery-<version>-win-x64-setup.exe` | `ScienceDiscovery-<version>-mac-<arch>.dmg`, plus `.zip` as the update carrier and a per-arch `latest-mac.yml` |
| Signing | Current version is unsigned. The next version may add Azure Trusted Signing (OIDC short-lived credentials in CI, no certificate on disk). Identity validation is officially ~3–5 business days and can stretch to weeks if materials are bounced, so the application has to start early. | Public distribution requires Developer ID + notarization (notarytool) + stapling. Internal beta may ship ad-hoc with `xattr -cr` guidance, switching to the notarized chain as soon as it is ready. Apple account and certificate lead time applies. |
| Runtime pinning | — | The macOS build needs a pinned runtime manifest: CPython (both architectures), uv (mac wheel), micromamba (osx-arm64/osx-64), and the starter environment, all by version and hash. Today the manifest pins Linux only. |
| Distribution | All downloads are GitHub Releases assets. The website `/install` page is the primary entry point and the Releases page the secondary one; both link the same assets. No domestic object storage or custom domain. Plugin packages ship the same way. | `/install` shows two download cards and pre-selects the architecture by user agent, with manual override. |
| Updates | electron-updater reading Releases assets, stable channel only to start, `latest.yml` + blockmap for delta updates. | The zip is the update carrier: electron-updater downloads the notarized zip, replaces the `.app`, and restarts. The DMG is not part of the update flow. |
| Update-source stability | The update URL is fixed from the first public release, because installed apps have it baked in. | same |
| Interception | SmartScreen: unsigned cold starts are accepted for now, with documented "More info → Run anyway" guidance. | Gatekeeper: notarization plus stapling removes the prompt entirely; no user guidance is needed once that chain is live. |

## First run

- Three-step wizard: data directory → model configuration (preset provider → API key → live connectivity test) → done.
- On Windows the wizard goes through direct execution only: no environment preparation, no WSL involvement.
- On macOS the final step folds in the sandbox self-check. A failure shows a specific error page with diagnostics and a way to submit them, and **does not** let the user into the main UI. Ordinary users never see this page.
- Data directory defaults: Windows splits by provider — direct execution uses `%LocalAppData%`, WSL uses ext4 inside the instance for I/O performance — with a custom option and a free-space check. macOS uses `~/Library/Application Support/ScienceDiscovery` and offers a one-time migration when a source-mode `~/.sciencediscovery-data` is found.
- Model keys: Windows stores them with DPAPI, because `0600` file permissions mean nothing on NTFS. macOS keeps the existing AES-256-GCM + `0600` scheme.
- The access token is injected before the page loads; a token entry page appears only as a 401 fallback.
- Background work during first run (environment unpacking, stack start) reports real progress by file and byte count, with conservative time estimates, and gates the next step on a self-check.

## Security baseline

Shared:

- Workspace-directory allowlist; network calls require explicit authorization (egress denied by default, allowlist to permit, refusals recorded).
- A persistent badge in the UI states the execution mode.
- Supply chain: updates over HTTPS with integrity checks (sha512 in the Windows update manifest; same-chain signing and notarization for the macOS update zip). **Once signing is live, no unsigned version is published again**, and a signature-identity change is covered by a dual-identity transition window.

Windows direct execution (no sandbox):

- The permission mode is locked to "ask on dangerous operations" and the user cannot switch to "always allow". This is enforced server-side, so a modified frontend cannot bypass it. Usability is unaffected: safe operations never prompt, and dangerous-operation prompts offer "allow once" or "allow matching", so approving a class of operation stops repeated prompts.
- The stack is not multi-instance: fixed ports, loopback-only listeners; a port occupied by an unknown process is reported honestly rather than worked around.

## Compatibility

Windows:

| OS | Direct execution | WSL plugin |
|---|---|---|
| Windows 11 22H2+ | yes | yes (inbox component; mirrored networking available) |
| Windows 10 2004+ | yes | yes (`wsl --install --no-distribution`) |
| Windows 10 1909 and older | yes, degraded | no — explicit "not installable" message |

macOS: 13+ on arm64 (mainline — CI smoke and e2e run here) and 13+ on x64 (package plus lightweight validation); macOS 12 and older unsupported, matching the existing source-mode floor.

Known environmental constraints to handle explicitly:

- Windows path length (260 characters) versus deep Python package trees: guide toward a shallow data directory, keep the environment root shallow, truncate over-long filenames.
- Windows antivirus tools interrupting file writes during install and update, producing incomplete installs; unsigned builds add SmartScreen on top. Document allowlisting and maintain a known-issues library.
- Windows defaulting to GBK on Chinese systems: every script must specify UTF-8 explicitly.
- macOS App Translocation and the quarantine flag before notarization: both are resolved by signing, notarizing, and stapling.
- Missing Apple Silicon builds for a minority of packages: guide users to pip.

## Non-functional budgets

| Metric | Budget | Target |
|---|---|---|
| First run, fresh install to usable main UI | ≤1 min, both platforms | Windows ~30 s on SSD (environment ships in the package, so the cost is unpacking plus stack start); macOS near-instant |
| Packaged stack start | fast | port 4310 healthy within 30 s, both platforms |
| Minor-version update | delta only | Windows blockmap delta; macOS zip delta |
| WSL plugin install | real progress, conservative estimate | rootfs import plus dependency check within a fixed bound once the first release has data |

Memory: on Windows with the WSL plugin active, write `.wslconfig` limits (4 GB / 4 processors, adjustable in the wizard) so `vmmem` cannot take half the host. Direct execution has no `vmmem`. macOS needs no mechanism. The ~200 MB Electron shell is accepted on both.

## Process model

Three kinds of process, managed by one Electron main process:

| Process | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| Electron main | Native window and OS integration (Windows: tray and system menu; macOS: application menu, Cmd+Q / Cmd+W); backend lifecycle (probe, start, clean shutdown); injects the access token before page load. |
| Renderer | The existing web UI; on first run it renders the bundled local wizard page first, then the main UI. |
| Backend stack | adapter (Python front door) + API (Node, business logic) + runner (code execution: the routing target on Windows, the sandbox execution point on macOS); memory-graph, evolve, and JiuwenSwarm start on demand. |

Startup: renderer wizard first (it needs no backend) → health probe every 3 s, reusing an already-healthy stack left over from a crash instead of starting a second one → otherwise start the stack → load the UI once the stack is healthy. Request path: page → adapter `:4310` → API `:4410` → runner `:4311`. Shutdown waits for running tasks, then stops only the children this process started; a reused stack is left alone. On Windows the window minimizes to the tray by default and closing it asks for confirmation when tasks are running; on macOS closing the window keeps the application and the backend alive, matching the backend semantics that a run continues after the page is closed.

Updates: checked at startup and every 6 hours; notify, download only on confirmation, never silently upgrade in the background. Installation first waits for running tasks and confirms all child processes have exited.

## Expected new components

- `client/shell/` — the Electron shell (shared; main process branches on platform, preload handles token injection and wizard IPC, `wizard.html` and `fallback.html` are platform-neutral).
- `packages/execution-router/` — the Windows execution-provider routing layer (no macOS counterpart).
- `packages/*/platform/` — per-package platform adapters (win32 and darwin side by side, single entry point, module boundaries enforced), e.g. a secret protector that uses DPAPI on Windows and AES-256-GCM + `0600` on macOS.
- `packages/sandbox-capability/` — extend the existing probe and runtime manifest with macOS entries.
- `scripts/start-stack.mjs` — packaged stack entry point, plus `stack-platform.mjs` for platform differences.
- `build/assemble-backend.mjs`, `build/resources/`, `build/rootfs/` — backend assembly (Windows x64 and per-arch macOS), the extraResources volume, and the trimmed WSL rootfs build (Windows only).
- `scripts/binary-release/runtimes.json` — add the darwin section.
- `.github/workflows/` — add Windows and `macos-14` (arm64) jobs for packaging (macOS including signing and notarization) and platform regression.

## Delivery milestones

| Milestone | Platform | Exit criteria |
|---|---|---|
| M1 | Windows | Download page → setup.exe → wizard → complete a small task with SD, never touching WSL. |
| M2 | Windows | On a machine without WSL: one-click sandbox install from the plugin center → run a sandboxed task → uninstall and fall back. |
| M3 | macOS | Source stack plus shell loading 4310 (backend ready, sandbox native — if the shell runs, this works). |
| M4 | macOS | Signed and notarized DMG, double-click to use: fresh Mac → download → drag install → wizard → complete a small task with no Gatekeeper prompt at any point. |

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Windows: a fresh machine installs and completes a task without WSL installed.
- [ ] Windows: the sandbox plugin installs in one click, resumes after interruption, and can be uninstalled cleanly.
- [ ] Windows: direct execution cannot be switched to "always allow", and the lock holds when the client is modified.
- [ ] macOS: a signed, notarized DMG opens with no Gatekeeper prompt and no `xattr` workaround.
- [ ] macOS: when Seatbelt is unavailable, startup fails closed with diagnostics instead of running unsandboxed.
- [ ] Both: first run reaches a usable UI within the stated budget on a fresh install.
- [ ] Both: an update lands as a delta, never silently, and never while a task is running.
- [ ] Both: the shell loads the existing `apps/web` build — no forked frontend.
- [ ] Both: quitting leaves no orphaned stack processes, and a reused stack is not stopped.

## Open questions

1. Is an Apple Developer identity available to the project for Developer ID signing and notarization? Public macOS distribution cannot ship without it, and the account lead time is real.
2. Do we start the Azure Trusted Signing application now so the next Windows version can be signed? If the answer is yes, the application has to begin ahead of the release.
3. When do we add a distribution path that is reliable from mainland China? GitHub asset downloads are workable but not dependable, and the update source is fixed once the first public release ships.
4. The shell is expected to live outside the main repository's git history. Is that acceptable to the maintainers, or should it live in-tree?
5. Telemetry is scoped to a minimal, in-app-disableable set with a published collection list (install success rate, first-run completion, Windows provider distribution and plugin install step outcomes, macOS architecture distribution, Seatbelt probe failure rate). Does that list pass review?

401.author: wyhohyw
401.body:
## Background

After a long-running tool execution fails, an Agent often has to infer completed work, reusable outputs, and possible continuation points from free-form logs. Execution state and logs alone do not provide a consistent basis for deciding where to continue.

Support recovery of failed long-running tasks: after the failure is addressed and the prerequisites are verified, the Agent can reuse completed results and continue from a supported recovery point, reducing unnecessary recomputation.

A shared, optional recovery metadata contract for tools and task adapters provides the supporting evidence. The LLM uses it to decide the next action; the framework persists and exposes it alongside the existing execution record, reusing existing execution tools and permission checks.

## Requested functionality

- Identify the original execution and expose completed stages or work units, the failed stage, and the failure reason when the task adapter can determine them.
- Reference reusable outputs and available task checkpoints using stable artifact/file/version identifiers where supported. Distinguish verified completed outputs from partial files.
- Explicitly report whether continuation is supported, unsupported, or unknown, including available continuation entry points and required inputs when supported.
- Describe conditions that must be checked before continuation, such as original execution termination, input/configuration changes, environment availability, and output validity.
- Preserve the metadata across refresh/reconnect and make it available through existing execution inspection and Agent tool results. Keep existing tools without recovery metadata compatible.
- Let the Agent inspect the evidence and choose repair, continuation, or a fresh attempt through existing execution tools and permission checks. Metadata itself must not automatically launch a replacement task.

The exact schema should follow the existing execution/tool-result architecture. Framework code should remain independent of specific scientific pipeline stages; task adapters supply domain-specific recovery information.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A shared, documented optional recovery metadata contract is available to long-running tools/task adapters.
- [ ] At least one supported long-running task adapter or representative test fixture demonstrates completed work, failed work, reusable result/checkpoint references, and continuation prerequisites.
- [ ] The Agent can retrieve persisted metadata after reconnecting and use it to identify a supported continuation point without relying solely on free-form logs.
- [ ] Unsupported or unknown recovery capability is explicit; the framework does not invent missing checkpoints or treat file existence alone as proof of completion.
- [ ] A running or unknown original execution is not automatically resubmitted because recovery metadata was returned.
- [ ] Tests cover supported/unsupported/unknown continuation, partial or invalid outputs, changed prerequisites, and persistence/readback.

## Scope and related work

- #398 covers reconnecting to the original NPU task, recovering its state/results, and avoiding duplicate submissions. This issue supplies structured evidence for Agent decisions after a confirmed failure.
- #278 covers in-conversation configuration and task continuation.
- This first version does not include arbitrary Agent-history rollback, restoration of process/NPU memory, or implementing model-specific computational checkpointing. Actual computational continuation depends on task-program support.
- Target release: **v0.3.0, October 30, 2026**, tracked in #249.

---

## 需求背景

长任务执行失败后，Agent 往往需要从自由文本日志中推断哪些工作已经完成、哪些结果可以复用、可以从哪里继续。仅有执行状态和日志，缺少统一的信息契约支撑这些判断。

支持长任务失败后的恢复：处理失败原因并确认接续前提后，Agent 能复用已完成结果，从受支持的恢复点继续，减少不必要的重复计算。

工具和任务适配器提供共享、可选的结构化恢复信息，作为上述能力的支撑。LLM 根据这些证据决定下一步；框架负责随现有执行记录持久化和提供查询，复用已有执行工具与权限检查。

## 期望功能

- 标识原执行；任务适配器能够确定时，返回已完成阶段或工作单元、失败阶段及失败原因。
- 通过受支持的稳定产物／文件／版本标识，引用可复用结果和任务检查点，区分已验证的完整结果与未完成文件。
- 明确返回可续跑、不支持续跑或能力未知；支持时给出可用续跑入口及所需输入。
- 描述接续前需要检查的条件，例如原执行已经结束、输入和配置变化、环境可用性及结果有效性。
- 刷新或重连后仍能通过现有执行查询和 Agent 工具结果获取这些信息；兼容不提供恢复信息的已有工具。
- Agent 根据证据选择修复、接续或重新执行，沿用现有执行工具及权限检查；返回恢复信息本身不自动启动替代任务。

具体字段设计应复用现有执行记录和工具结果架构。框架保持通用，由任务适配器提供具体业务阶段及恢复信息。

## 验收标准

- [ ] 提供有文档说明、可选的统一恢复信息契约，供长任务工具／适配器使用。
- [ ] 至少一个受支持的长任务适配器或有代表性的测试夹具，能够展示已完成工作、失败工作、可复用结果／检查点引用及接续前提。
- [ ] 重连后 Agent 能读取持久化信息，识别受支持的接续点，无须仅依赖自由文本日志推断。
- [ ] 不支持或能力未知时明确返回；框架不虚构检查点，也不把文件存在直接当作步骤已完成。
- [ ] 原执行仍在运行或结果未知时，不会因为返回恢复信息而自动重复提交。
- [ ] 测试覆盖支持／不支持／未知续跑能力、部分或无效结果、前提条件变化及持久化读取。

## 范围与关联

- #398 负责找回原 NPU 任务、恢复状态和结果、避免重复提交；本需求为确认失败后的 Agent 接续决策提供结构化证据。
- #278 负责对话内配置和任务接续。
- 首版不包含任意历史 Agent 状态回滚、进程／NPU 内存恢复，也不代替具体模型实现计算检查点。实际计算续跑依赖任务程序支持。
- 目标版本：**2026 年 10 月 30 日 v0.3.0**，在 #249 跟踪。

## Summary

Follow-up from [#276](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/276) (closed). Recovery `direct_code` when sandbox is unavailable on local (#361) and reachable remote (#363) is done. This Issue tracks **agent-first direct execution**: the Agent may choose direct execution when the user asks to skip the sandbox (or the Agent judges sandbox unsuitable). The framework should **suggest** sandbox by default and keep the `direct_code` consent gate — not hard-require “sandbox already unavailable” before direct tools can be used.

## Background / decisions (from #276)

- Unreachable Runner / SSH repair: **out of scope** (user/network admin).
- Managed environment: **Agent decides**; ask the user when needed; **no** complex Settings for this.
- Architecture target recorded on #276: drop precondition `Runner reachable + sandbox unavailable` as the only path into `requirePrivilege({ action: "direct_code" })` → user allow → `run_direct_*`.

## Goal

Give the Agent policy control over sandbox vs direct; framework = suggestion + authorization, not a failure-only gate.

## Acceptance

1. Agent can initiate direct-execution consent while the sandbox is still available, when the user requested skip-sandbox or the Agent judges sandbox unsuitable (prompt/tool guidance makes sandbox the default preference).
2. Hard gate removed/replaced: reachable Runner (or local) still required; unreachable → clear failure + admin guidance; **no** requirement that sandbox be unavailable to *request* `direct_code`.
3. `direct_code` stays separate from sandbox `code` Always Allow (no silent carry-over); consent remains per command + scope + Agent run; no auto-replay / silent execute from chat text alone.
4. Sandbox tools and direct tools are peers; sandbox-failure errors may *suggest* direct but must not be the only way direct appears.
5. Tests/journey cover: user-predeclared direct while sandbox still “ready”; recovery path when sandbox unavailable still works; unreachable runner still blocked without SSH-maintenance feature.
6. Docs/prompt/tool copy updated for “prefer sandbox; direct needs explicit user consent.”

## Non-goals

- SSH maintenance for unreachable hosts
- Complex Settings for managed-environment presets
- Closing product gaps already accepted as out of scope on #276

## Related

- Parent: #276
- Delivered recovery: #361, #363

### 🚀 Background Description


Currently, the SD chat interface does not display the timestamp of sent messages, making it difficult for users to determine how long a task has been running or how long they have been waiting. Therefore, it is recommended to add message timestamps in the format "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS" (e.g., 2026-10-09 15:32:43) to the chat interface.

### Design Ideas

None

420.author: HongyeZhou
420.body:
## Problem and user outcome

Researchers need to retrieve domain-specific scientific data through MCP and use it in traceable ScienceDiscovery workflows. Literature search alone does not satisfy this need: the objects are expression datasets, bioactivity measurements, variant assertions, and protein structures.

Provide supported, discoverable connections to **GEO, ChEMBL, ClinVar, RCSB PDB, and AlphaFold Protein Structure Database**, with reliable retrieval, explicit data boundaries, and provenance that survives downstream analysis.

## Context and existing implementation

Request inspired by this article: https://x.com/servasyy_ai/article/2112052770287284550
Related project documentation: https://aipoch.com/docs/guides/connectors/

Source inspection of ScienceDiscovery at baseline `0d31e155` found existing MCP implementations for GEO, ChEMBL, ClinVar, and PDB in `services/gateway/src/sciencediscovery_gateway/public_biomed_mcp.py`, plus manifests in `packages/mcp-sources/src/public-biomed.ts`. UniProt, Ensembl, and Reactome provide additional reusable patterns. No built-in AlphaFold DB adapter was found in that inspection.

This is a request to complete and validate domain database support, reusing existing adapters. It does not assume these databases are entirely unsupported. The baseline assessment was static inspection, not a live end-to-end availability test; recheck the target version before implementation.

## Requested scope

| Database | Required user-facing capabilities | Domain details to preserve |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GEO | Search studies, retrieve study/sample metadata, discover actual processed/supplementary files, and download selected analysis-ready data | GSE/GSM/GPL identifiers, organism, sample conditions, platform, and whether data are raw counts, normalized values, or other processed data |
| ChEMBL | Search molecules/targets, retrieve bioactivity measurements with useful filters, and perform similarity searches | Molecule/target/assay IDs, assay type, organism, relation, value, units, confidence, and source references |
| ClinVar | Search/lookup variants and retrieve individual clinical assertions | VCV/RCV/SCV identifiers where applicable, assembly, condition, review status, dates, and conflicting submissions |
| RCSB PDB | Search/lookup experimental structures and download supported structure files | PDB ID, experimental method, resolution where applicable, chains/entities, ligands, and source/version metadata |
| AlphaFold DB | Retrieve available predictions by protein accession and download model/confidence files when available | UniProt accession, model identifier/version, source URLs, and confidence information |

AlphaFold DB retrieval is separate from running AlphaFold prediction software. New prediction compute infrastructure is outside this request. PubMed and other literature databases are also outside this scope.

## Integration requirements

- Reuse the MCP client, connector selection, permission/audit, and artifact download mechanisms. Prefer official provider APIs behind MCP adapters; do not require providers to expose MCP themselves.
- Make supported sources and operations discoverable, with setup instructions and any credential requirements. Enable the source for the intended Session and support both Inspector validation and Agent use.
- Return structured domain data and standard evidence records with stable identifiers, source links, retrieval time, and provider version/release when available. Retain source caveats and attribution.
- A generic custom MCP connection currently preserves raw/structured content but produces empty standardized `records`; calling a tool successfully alone must not count as complete evidence integration.
- Transfer large datasets and structure files through governed artifact jobs, with source metadata and integrity checks. Keep file bytes out of model context and distinguish a proposed download from a completed, verified artifact.
- Handle pagination, provider rate limits, timeouts, invalid identifiers, missing records/files, and partial failures explicitly. Do not silently present a capped subset as the complete dataset.
- Document scientific limits: GEO standard matrix/SOFT candidate paths do not enumerate all supplementary files; not every expression matrix is suitable for count-based analysis; ClinVar submissions can conflict; experimental and predicted structures must remain distinguishable.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] On the target version, document the existing capability and remaining gap for each of the five databases.
- [ ] All five sources can be configured/enabled and successfully called from the intended Session; tool inputs and results are inspectable and audited.
- [ ] Each database has a representative live provider validation with recorded identifiers, commands/steps, expected results, and actual results. Record unavailable-provider cases as blocked rather than passed.
- [ ] GEO: discover actual files for a public study, retrieve relevant sample annotations, and download/verify a real selected matrix. Validate its data type and dimensions before downstream analysis; report when count-based analysis is inappropriate.
- [ ] ChEMBL: retrieve a target/molecule-linked activity set with explicit assay/measurement constraints, preserving units and relations, and verify pagination or clearly disclosed limits.
- [ ] ClinVar: retrieve assertions and preserve conflicting classifications/review status without reducing them to one unsupported consensus.
- [ ] PDB: retrieve an experimental structure, complete a verified CIF/PDB download, and demonstrate that a downstream analysis step can read the artifact and inspect its metadata.
- [ ] AlphaFold DB: retrieve a known available prediction by accession, verify a model download and available confidence metadata, and clearly identify it as predicted.
- [ ] Returned evidence and downloaded artifacts retain their source identifiers/URLs and retrieval metadata in subsequent analysis outputs.
- [ ] Automated tests cover domain result normalization and representative missing-record, malformed-input, rate-limit, and download-failure paths. Product-level validation covers connector selection, Inspector/Agent execution, and completed artifacts; mocked success alone is insufficient.
- [ ] User documentation describes supported operations, limitations, configuration, and reproducible examples for each source.

Implementation may be split into linked changes, but this feature remains open until the full five-database acceptance scope is verified.

## Problem
The `CodeCheck (GitCode)` check run on GitHub PRs only says "GitCode labelled the merge request `ci-failed`" and links to the GitCode MR. It doesn't name the failing rule or file. The GitCode MR page/API is not reachable for every contributor or reviewer (WAF/login). So authors end up writing "CodeCheck is ignored" (e.g. #421, also failing on #412 and #391), and reviewers can't tell whether a failure comes from the PR.

## Expected
When CodeCheck fails, the GitHub check-run output lists the failing checker/rule, file:line and message (or a stable public log link), so authors and reviewers can act without GitCode access.

## Verification cases
1. **Failure details mirrored**
   - Preconditions: a PR whose head introduces a known CodeCheck violation (e.g. a lint rule the GitCode pipeline enforces).
   - Steps: push; wait for the sync; open the `CodeCheck (GitCode)` check run on GitHub.
   - Expected / pass: `output.summary` or `output.text` names the rule, file:line and message; conclusion `failure`.
2. **Clean head**
   - Preconditions: a PR with no violations.
   - Steps: push; open the check run.
   - Expected / pass: conclusion `success`; no stale failure text from an earlier head.
3. **Infra failure isn't shown as a code failure (negative)**
   - Preconditions: the GitCode pipeline fails for an infra reason (timeout/sync error).
   - Steps: trigger; open the check run.
   - Expected / pass: output says it's an infra/sync failure, not a code violation, and links to a retry path.
4. **No secret leakage (security)**
   - Preconditions: a pipeline log that contains tokens/env.
   - Steps: mirror the failure details.
   - Expected / pass: mirrored text contains no tokens, cookies or internal URLs with credentials.

## Context
Refs #421, Refs #385. Seen at #421 head f494792 (GitCode MR !296) and #412 head 29e724a.
422.title: CI: surface GitCode CodeCheck failure details on the GitHub check run

433.author: zy95-12
433.body:
## 背景 / 输入

在本地 ScienceDiscovery（main 源码 serve，`http://127.0.0.1:4310`）用 NatureBench 论文复现 case：

- Case：`s43588-024-00689-2`（meK-means / multimodal clustering）
- 会话：`93f897ca-cefe-4e7b-932d-8339cbef1459`（项目「NatureBench meK-means 复现」）
- 宿主侧把任务数据以**绝对路径软链**放进 session workspace：
  - `naturebench_data` → `/workspace/NatureBench/data/naturebench_data/tasks/s43588-024-00689-2/problem/data`
  - `CGP_2023_ref` → `/workspace/CGP_2023`
- Agent 在沙箱内执行 `run.py` 读 loom / 作者代码

相关 run：`8164ed2d-8b42-4d67-9d4b-e47c12ce0f7e`（第一轮，约 23.6 min，仅 smoke）

## 问题是什么

会话沙箱里 `/workspace` 是 **session workspace 的 bind mount**，会遮蔽宿主上的 `/workspace/...`。因此指向宿主绝对路径的软链在沙箱内**解析失败**，真实 loom 不可达。

结果：Agent 只能合成 loom 做端到端 smoke，**真实 `output/{cl3,cl5,mop_*}/predictions.npy` 第一轮全部缺失**；报告写「blocked / NOT produced」。

## 我们怎么规避的

在**宿主**（沙箱外）把数据 materialize 成会话内相对目录，并删掉绝对软链：

```bash
cd …/sessions/<sid>/workspace
cp -a /workspace/NatureBench/.../problem/data nb_data
# 去掉指向宿主 /workspace 的断链软链
rm -f naturebench_data CGP_2023_ref
DATA_DIR=nb_data python run.py --data-dir nb_data
```

续跑后 cl3 / cl5 / mop_sc 真实 predictions 才落盘。

## 期望应该是什么样

1. 往 session workspace 放数据时，产品应 **materialize 或相对路径化**（或官方 `workspace_transfer`），**不要**依赖指向宿主绝对路径的软链。
2. UI / API 上传或「挂载外部目录」若最终进沙箱，应在创建时校验：沙箱内 `ls` 可读；失败则明确报错，而不是让 Agent 默默落到合成数据。
3. 文档写清：沙箱可见路径规则（相对 workspace、禁止宿主绝对软链）。

## 证据

- 第一轮报告结论与 `naturebench_data` → `/workspace/NatureBench/...` 软链
- 续跑 materialize `nb_data/` 后 cl3 `(902,)`、cl5 `(3918,)`、mop_sc `(5693,)` 真实 npy 成功
433.title: Bug: session sandbox breaks absolute host symlinks for task data (NatureBench reproduce)

434.author: zy95-12
434.body:
## 背景 / 输入

同一 NatureBench 复现会话 `93f897ca-cefe-4e7b-932d-8339cbef1459`：

- 续跑 run：`84d71b8a-77dd-42a7-bc81-15e326b14cb1`（约 14.1 min，`completed`）
- Agent 顺序跑实例：`cl3` → `cl5` → `mop_sc`（EM 估计约 50–60 min）
- 通过 `tools/run_instances.sh` / `tools/run_timed.py` 拉起后台 `python run.py --instances mop_sc`

## 问题是什么

1. **Run / turn 已 `completed`，但 CPU 作业仍在跑**（孤儿进程）。监控时可见 PID 仍以 ~100% CPU 跑 mop_sc，而 API run 状态早已结束。
2. Agent 用「45 分钟定时器再回来」这类自我约定结束 turn，框架**没有跨 turn 的长任务/作业跟踪**，用户与监控只能靠 `ps` 发现。
3. 后台 `print` **块缓冲**时，日志长时间不增长，看起来像卡死（见关联 issue：重定向日志缓冲）。

## 我们怎么规避的

- 宿主侧继续 `ps` / 等 `output/mop_sc/predictions.npy` 落盘（约 26.5 min 后成功）。
- 明确 **不**再起第二轮 SD run 抢同一作业；mop_sn 因体量过大主动 deferred 并杀掉误启动的排队。

## 期望应该是什么样

1. 沙箱/主机上的长命令应挂到 **可查询的 job / process 句柄**（run 级或 session 级）：run 结束 ≠ 计算结束时，UI 仍显示「后台作业进行中」。
2. Agent 结束 turn 时若仍有未收尾子进程，应默认：提示、挂起、或要求显式 `detach`；不要静默孤儿化。
3. 支持「续接同一作业」的会话语义（resume / await job），避免 Agent 用墙钟定时器假装调度。

## 证据

- Run `84d71b8a-…` `completed` 后 PID `647972` 仍在跑 `run.py --instances mop_sc`
- 最终 mop_sc：`predictions.npy` shape `(5693,)`，`wall≈1587.7s`，peak RSS≈953MB
434.title: Usability: long CPU jobs become orphans when agent turn/run completes (no cross-turn job tracking)

435.body:
## 背景 / 输入

NatureBench 复现会话开启 Automatic review（`reviewerAutomaticReviewEnabled=true`，`reviewMode=auto`，specialist=`quick`）。

- 第一轮 run 结束后主交付（4 实例真实 `predictions.npy`）**缺失**，报告写 blocked
- Artifact：`REPRODUCTION_REPORT.md` 触发 `reviewer_checkpoint` → **PASSED / ACCEPT_AND_PROCEED**，findings 空
- 审阅 JSON 仅 citation 类 check（与文献 case 的 Quick 行为一致，参见 #414）
- 续跑产出真实 cl3/cl5/mop_sc npy 并改写报告后，**未自动重审**；磁盘上旧 ACCEPT 仍对应「blocked」叙事

## 问题是什么

1. **交付物缺失仍 ACCEPT**：复现任务的成功标准是 `output/{instance}/predictions.npy`，Quick 几乎只看 citation 格式，拦不住「没复现成功」。
2. **报告/审阅不同步**：工件已更新，Automatic review 不因新版本自动失效或重跑；用户看到的仍是过期 ACCEPT。

## 我们怎么规避的

- 不以 review ACCEPT 作为复现成功判据；宿主侧用 numpy 核对 npy shape / K，并手改 `REPRODUCTION_REPORT.md` 写清真实现状。
- 体验结论单独记录，不依赖审阅绿勾。

## 期望应该是什么样

1. 复现 / 计算类报告：Quick 之外至少校验「声明的交付路径是否存在、非空」；缺失则 **不能** ACCEPT_AND_PROCEED。
2. Artifact 新版本落盘后：旧 review 标记 stale，或自动触发重审；UI 明确「审阅对应的是哪一版」。
3. 与 #414（文献 claim fidelity）区分但可共用：按 artifact 类型选审查准则，而不是一律 citation-only。

## 相关

436.body:
## 背景 / 输入

NatureBench 复现会话在 run 前已通过 API 将 `approvalMode` 设为 `always_allow`：

```http
PATCH /api/sessions/{sessionId}
{"approvalMode":"always_allow"}
```

随后 Agent 大量调用工具（读文件、装依赖、跑 python、写报告等）。日志：`jiuwenswarm.log`。

## 问题是什么

即便会话级 `always_allow`，运行中仍出现大量 **`allow_once` 且 `persisted=False`** 风格的授权记录（约百余次量级），审批噪声大、不粘滞。长复现任务的可观测性被权限流水淹没；也与用户对「Always allow = 本会话不再追问」的心智模型不符。

（权限文案/网络同意相关体验另见 #392、#393。）

## 我们怎么规避的

- 仍设 `always_allow`，减少 UI 卡死概率。
- 监控与成功判据改看 workspace 文件与 run 状态，不依赖权限流水是否「干净」。

## 期望应该是什么样

1. `always_allow` 应对该 session（或同 permission epoch）的同类工具调用真正粘滞，而不是每次 `allow_once` + `persisted=False`。
2. 日志/UI 在 always_allow 下折叠或汇总授权，避免百级噪音。
3. 文档写清：哪些动作仍会突破 always_allow（若有硬例外），并与设置文案一致。

## 相关

- #392 Permission card: "Allow same type" is unclear
- #393 Resume after a sandbox network block needs three consecutive approvals

## 背景 / 输入

在 ScienceDiscovery 沙箱 / science-env 中复现 meK-means（Monod `mminference`）：

444.author: zhaozhaozz
444.body:
`pnpm ci:ut` starts one JiuwenSwarm instance for the whole slice and then runs every API test file one at a time. Unit tests should start independently and run in parallel. Only a test that declares a real JiuwenSwarm instance should use one, and those tests should take that instance from a single queue.

## What happens now

`scripts/with-jiuwenswarm.sh` installs the pinned JiuwenSwarm, starts one instance and one adapter, and exports `SCIENCE_AGENT_EXECUTOR=jiuwenswarm` plus `SCIENCE_AGENT_ADAPTER_URL` to every process in the slice. One instance has one tool server, so a second adapter would take it from the first.

`createApiServer` reads that process environment. When the variables are set, starting the server syncs web settings to the shared adapter (up to five attempts, three seconds apart). The UT scheduler then marks every file under `services/api/` as one resource, so those files never overlap. The default worker count is 2, and the scheduler rejects a count above 4.

Of the 112 API test files, two wait on a real gateway turn (`services/api/src/server.test.ts` and `services/api/src/run-cancel.test.ts`). Five more start the production server and reach the adapter only because the environment is process-wide (`dashboard.test.ts`, `mcp/source-api.test.ts`, `model-usage-api.test.ts`, `npu-selection-api.test.ts`, `ssh-host-api.test.ts`). The other 105 do not start that server. On one warm run the API lane took 519 seconds, which was the entire UT test wall clock, while the machine had 14 CPUs. GitHub Actions runs this job on a public `ubuntu-latest` runner.

Cases tagged `status:unreviewed` are already outside the plan. They stay there.

## Required behavior

- A unit test that does not declare a JiuwenSwarm instance starts on its own and may run at the same time as other such tests. It must not see `SCIENCE_AGENT_EXECUTOR=jiuwenswarm` or the shared adapter URL, even if it boots `createApiServer`.
- A test that needs a real instance declares that on the test. The directory of the file is not a declaration.
- The UT layer owns one generic startup and one queue for that instance. Declaring tests run on it one at a time. The queue covers only the declaring test, not the other tests in the same file.
- Non-declaring tests use as many workers as a public GitHub-hosted `ubuntu-latest` runner can sustain. Local `pnpm ci:ut` and the UT job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` use that same number. Do not take the default from the workstation CPU count. Public `ubuntu-latest` runners have 4 vCPUs and 16 GB of RAM; confirm the current size and pin one shared default. If that width is killed for memory, lower the shared default and record why. The two environments must not diverge.
- Do not weaken an assertion, delete a test, or move a `status:unreviewed` case back into the plan to make the run green.

## Done when

- A scheduler test shows non-declaring work overlapping up to the shared worker count, and declaring work never overlapping, including across files.
- `pnpm ci:ut` passes at that worker count, and the GitHub Actions UT job runs the same entry point without a second worker override.
- The pull request names the worker count, lists the tests that declare an instance, and reports the UT numbers.

## Problem and user impact

When a user clicks the download button for an MCP-provided artifact in the conversation, the download card changes to **Waiting for approval** (Chinese: **等待审批**), but does not explain who should approve or provide an approval action/link. The user cannot discover how to proceed.

The pending permission is intended to be decided by the user in the current Session, not by the database provider or a separate administrator.

## Reported reproduction

1. In the frontend, retrieve a scientific database entry that exposes a downloadable artifact, for example RCSB PDB `1ATP` through the PDB MCP connector.
2. Use a Session permission policy that requires explicit artifact-download consent, without a matching existing grant.
3. Click the artifact's download/prepare button.
4. Observe **Waiting for approval**, with no clear approval entry point or indication that the current user must act.

Expected: show the corresponding permission request immediately and make the approval action accessible from the pending download card. Identify that the current user is being asked to authorize a download to the Session workspace.

Actual: the download appears to wait on an unspecified approver; the user cannot locate an action to continue.

## Evidence and suspected cause

The user reported this behavior while manually testing the frontend. Their exact deployment/version has not been identified, and this report does not claim an independently reproduced browser failure on that deployment.

Source inspection at `bcd56b74bd9b79564e392da33e4977d94dd65034` (PR #441) found:

- `packages/artifact-manager/src/governed-download-manager.ts` creates an `artifact_download` permission request and associates its ID with an `awaiting_approval` artifact plan.
- `apps/web/src/App.tsx`: `prepareGovernedDownload()` creates the plan, then calls `refreshGovernedDownloads()`. That refresh fetches candidates, jobs, plans and invocations, but not permission requests. This can leave the newly created permission absent from frontend permission state, especially when the click happens outside an active Agent event stream.
- `apps/web/src/GovernedDownloadCards.tsx` renders pending plans as a “Waiting for approval” label, without an approval control or navigation to the linked permission request.
- The existing permission UI already supports allow-once, allow-matching and deny decisions; it should be reused rather than introducing a separate approval mechanism.

The missing permission-state refresh is a source-supported hypothesis, not a fully isolated browser root cause. Also check request attribution/grouping and timeline deduplication when reproducing: a request may exist but be rendered away from its download card.

## Suggested implementation

- Reconcile permission state after creating a manual artifact plan and whenever a pending download requires it; preserve active-Session guards and avoid duplicate permission cards.
- Provide an inline approval action or a reliable link/focus action to the associated permission card using `permissionRequestId`.
- Replace ambiguous waiting text with guidance that identifies the current user's required action, including localized English/Chinese copy.
- Reuse existing permission decisions and backend download advancement; do not bypass consent or automatically enable broad permissions.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Reproduce from the manual frontend download button on the target version, including after the Agent turn has finished.
- [ ] Under a consent-required policy, the related pending permission becomes visible without a page refresh, with an actionable entry point beside the download.
- [ ] The UI clearly explains who authorizes the download and what file/destination the permission covers.
- [ ] Allow once advances the linked plan to a real download job and a completed, verified artifact without another manual refresh.
- [ ] Deny produces a clear resolved state, with no misleading perpetual waiting indicator and no download started.
- [ ] Existing matching grants/allowed policies proceed without an unnecessary approval prompt.
- [ ] Reloading or switching Sessions restores the correct state without showing another Session's permission or duplicating requests.
- [ ] A browser regression covers manual click → visible approval → allow/deny → observable download outcome; backend assertions alone are insufficient.

Related: #420 and PR #441. This issue concerns the manual-download approval experience; it is not a report that the RCSB PDB provider is unavailable.

448.body:
## Problem and user outcome

Researchers need to verify that a PDB structure contains the same protein target and chemical compound as a ChEMBL activity record. Matching a structure title or compound name is insufficient: salt forms, different protein targets, and label/auth chain identifiers can produce incorrect cross-database associations.

The current PDB MCP connector supports full-text structure search, entry lookup and download preparation, but does not expose protein/nonpolymer entity or Chemical Component Dictionary (CCD) lookup tools. A representative ChEMBL → PDB validation therefore required direct official HTTPS calls outside MCP to complete identity verification.

Provide these operations through the existing PDB MCP connector, with structured evidence, source/version metadata and the existing governance/audit path.

## Existing evidence

Source-inspected candidate: `bcd56b74bd9b79564e392da33e4977d94dd65034` (PR #441). This describes that candidate, not an assertion that latest main has been independently reproduced.

A deterministic validation through the production Inspector/API successfully queried ChEMBL and PDB, downloaded a real mmCIF through governed artifact jobs, checked its SHA-256, and parsed actual coordinates. It did not establish a real-model automated Agent journey.

Positive example:

- Human EGFR: ChEMBL target `CHEMBL203`, UniProt `P00533`.
- Canertinib free molecule: `CHEMBL31965`; activity `121735`, IC50 = 74 nM, relation `=`, assay `CHEMBL683041`, assay type B, target confidence 9.
- Canertinib dihydrochloride: `CHEMBL545315`, parent `CHEMBL31965`; its complete InChIKey differs from the free molecule.
- PDB `9OS6`: protein entity 1 maps to `P00533`; nonpolymer entity 2 identifies CCD `A1CEA`.
- CCD `A1CEA` and free Canertinib share complete InChIKey `OMZCMEYTWSXEPZ-UHFFFAOYSA-N`.
- Protein label/auth chain is A/A; ligand label/auth chain is B/A. These naming systems must remain distinguishable.

Negative example:

- PDB `5VCW` contains Pelitinib, but protein entity 1 maps to MYT1 (`Q99640`), not EGFR (`P00533`). It must not be presented as an EGFR complex solely because Pelitinib has EGFR activity elsewhere.

Official records: https://www.rcsb.org/structure/9OS6 and https://www.rcsb.org/structure/5VCW.

## Requested MCP capabilities

Reuse the existing PDB adapter, source selection, transport, validation, Inspector, Agent tool registration, standard evidence normalization and permission/audit mechanisms. Suggested operations (names are implementation proposals):

1. `pdb_get_polymer_entity(pdb_id, entity_id)`
   - Entity description/type, source organism, UniProt/reference mappings, chain identifiers, sequence/coverage and construct/mutation information when available.
   - Preserve `label_asym_id` versus `auth_asym_id`; distinguish a kinase-domain construct from a full-length receptor.
2. `pdb_get_nonpolymer_entity(pdb_id, entity_id)`
   - Ligand/component ID, entity identity, label/auth chain mappings and provider cross-references when available.
3. `pdb_lookup_chemical_component(component_id)`
   - CCD name, formula/charge, InChI, complete InChIKey, available SMILES variants, and provider cross-database identifiers with mapping provenance.
   - Support valid extended component IDs such as five-character `A1CEA`, rather than assuming all CCD identifiers are three characters.

Also expose a discoverable way to enumerate the relevant entity IDs from a PDB entry. Reuse IDs already returned by entry lookup if sufficient; do not require users to guess entity IDs.

Equivalent bounded expansion of the existing entry lookup is acceptable if it satisfies these user-facing requirements without unbounded responses or extra requests for every ordinary lookup.

Official APIs used in the validation:

- `https://data.rcsb.org/rest/v1/core/polymer_entity/9OS6/1`
- `https://data.rcsb.org/rest/v1/core/nonpolymer_entity/9OS6/2`
- `https://data.rcsb.org/rest/v1/core/chemcomp/A1CEA`
- `https://data.rcsb.org/rest/v1/core/polymer_entity/5VCW/1`

## Data and integration requirements

- Return useful structured domain fields and nonempty standardized evidence records, including stable IDs, canonical URLs, retrieval times, attribution and provider version/revision when available.
- Preserve missing mappings explicitly. Missing UniProt/InChIKey must not be replaced by a name-based assertion of identity.
- Preserve salt/parent relationships and stereochemistry-aware complete identifiers. A parent relationship is not an assertion that salts or measured activity values are interchangeable.
- Treat covalent adducts, modified components or conflicting mappings as unresolved or explicitly qualified unless the evidence supports a stronger relationship.
- Reuse provider allowlists, rate limits, timeouts, input validation and error normalization; handle unknown entities/components and partial failures visibly.
- Provide concise model-facing summaries and retain complete provider content as traceable evidence rather than flooding model context with full sequences, synonym lists, cross-references or molfiles.
- Keep structure file transfer on existing governed artifact jobs, with checksums and source provenance.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] On the target version, document the existing gap and show the new operations in source discovery, Inspector schemas and the selected Session's Agent tools.
- [ ] Retrieve `9OS6` entity IDs through MCP, then verify protein entity 1 → UniProt `P00533` and nonpolymer entity 2 → CCD `A1CEA` through MCP.
- [ ] Retrieve CCD `A1CEA` through MCP and compare its complete InChIKey with ChEMBL `CHEMBL31965`; preserve the distinct salt record `CHEMBL545315` and its parent relationship.
- [ ] Preserve and display protein A/A and ligand B/A label/auth chain mappings without confusing protein and ligand instances.
- [ ] Retrieve `5VCW` protein identity through MCP and reject it as an EGFR complex because its target is `Q99640`, despite the compound-name association.
- [ ] Complete a selected mmCIF download via governed artifact jobs, verify it, read the actual file, and retain the cross-database evidence in saved analysis outputs.
- [ ] Run a product-level Agent journey that completes the identity checks using MCP tools, without direct HTTPS/web-fetch fallback for the requested metadata. Separately record Inspector, stub-model and real-model results; a successful direct API script alone is insufficient.
- [ ] Add meaningful coverage for extended CCD IDs, missing/invalid entities, missing chemical/protein mappings, rate-limit/timeout/partial-failure feedback, and label/auth chain distinctions.
- [ ] Add English/Chinese documentation describing supported operations, identity-matching limits and the reproducible positive/negative cases.

## Scope boundaries

This request exposes official metadata and supports verifiable identity comparisons. It does not add docking, affinity prediction, a universal chemical standardization engine, or permission bypasses. Geometric contacts do not establish potency, and IC50 is not Kd.

Related to #420 and PR #441. This is a concrete follow-up for the entity/chemical-identity lookup gap discovered during cross-database validation.

451.body:
## Background

A mocked end-to-end turn that changes the shared tool catalog spends a long time before the model is called. Measured on 2026-10-20, commit `d245cec8d9df52e0b3a99dd5bb236507ec73746d`, journey J3 (prepare a named environment and run one calculation):

- The scripted turn is two beats: one `run_shell` (stub delay 500 ms) and one closing text. Those beats, two rejected model calls, approval, and the shell finished in about 4 seconds.
- After `POST /agent/runs` and before the first `POST /mcp`, about 20 seconds pass. The run carried 44 tools. The MCP HTTP handshake itself, once started, was 7 ms (`platform_mcp_transport_open` to `platform_mcp_connect_ready`).
- After MCP is connected and before the first `chat/completions`, about 16–18 seconds pass. No model HTTP and no `/llm/default` call happen in that window.

Across the three mocked shards that day, the pre-MCP gap appeared on 21 runs (standard 12, research 8, literature 1) and added up to about 264 seconds. The post-connect, pre-model gap on those same runs added up to about 236 seconds. Most runs do not pay this, because their tool catalog does not change. Re-check both gaps on current `origin/main` before changing code; do not treat the old timestamps as a new measurement.

## Change 1: register tool permissions once

`AgentRunner.ensure_shared_tools` calls `_apply_approvals`, which sends `permissions.tools.update` once per tool. `gateway.rpc` opens a new management WebSocket for every call. On the Swarm side each update rewrites `config.yaml` under the config lock. A new shared-server generation name (`sci` plus ten digits) makes every `(server, tool)` key look new, so none of the 44 updates are skipped. `mcp.connect` runs only after that loop, and its live probe is the first `POST /mcp`.

Required behavior:

- Persist the approval map for one generation in one write, and do not open one management WebSocket per tool.
- If the shared tool catalog is unchanged, keep the MCP server that is already connected. Do not disconnect, register, or connect again.
- Leave the MCP handshake and live probe as they are.
- Keep each tool's approval level (`allow` / `ask` / `deny`). Do not widen access.
- Do not drop an in-flight tool call. A bare `mcp.disconnect` is global; reuse must not disconnect a server that still serves a run.
- Keep retiring inactive generations so `config.yaml` does not grow without bound.

## Change 2: skip unchanged per-turn prepare

The 16–18 seconds are work inside JiuwenSwarm after the tool server is connected and before the first model request. They are not time spent writing logs.

`_update_runtime_config` runs on every user message entering the runner. It already times stages (`cwd_seed`, `rail_setters`, `tools_for_mode`, `session_tools`, `prompt_for_mode`, `memory_tools`, and the smaller switches between them) and, after they finish, logs one line when the total is at least 50 ms:

```text
[AgentServer] runtime config applied: session_id=... mode=... total_ms=... <stage breakdown>
```

The threshold override is `JIUWENSWARM_SLOW_STAGE_MS`. A new session also logs `[AgentServer] session adapter created` with `create_instance_ms` and `start_interaction_ms`. After runtime config, `sync_agent_observability` runs: unchanged config is a no-op; a config change restarts the trajectory runtime and joins writer threads.

Required behavior:

- On one slow mocked journey with a new project and session and a single shell beat, capture those existing Swarm log lines. Do not add a second logging system to measure this.
- If `total_ms` is the bulk of the gap, skip the dominant stage when cwd, tools, prompt, and memory tools are unchanged for that session. Still run it when any of those inputs change.
- If `total_ms` is only tens or hundreds of milliseconds, the gap is session-adapter creation or observability sync. Shrink that work under the same rule: unchanged inputs are not prepared again.
- Do not delete the stage log line.
- Do not change the turn's result: same tools, same prompt when inputs changed, same shell cwd when the workspace changed.

If the captured log shows the time is necessary work that cannot be skipped without changing results, stop and report the line. Do not delete that work to make the clock smaller.

Ship a JiuwenSwarm change through the mechanism this repository already uses to patch JiuwenSwarm. Do not open a pull request against the upstream JiuwenSwarm or agent-core repositories from this issue.

## Look only: other mocked end-to-end waste

Look for other mocked end-to-end time that is startup or repeated rejected work, not the scripted beats. Report the cause, a rough saving, and whether removing it would change what a test proves. Do not implement those extras in this pull request.

Out of scope unless the report shows it is the same bug:

- HTTP 400 responses from the model gateway (unsupported parameters, images, token ceiling, `tool_choice`, `parallel_tool_calls=false`). The gateway body already states the reason; the access log keeps only the status. There were 216 such responses across the three shards. They return immediately.
- J3's environment clone, about 17 seconds, which is a separate step.
- The reviewer quiet-window wait.
- Deleting long journeys, raising end-to-end workers, or changing `slowMo`.
- Unit-test scheduling (tracked separately).

## Non-goals

- Do not weaken assertions or rewrite a test to avoid a real failure.
- Do not use the local trial port 4310 or its data directory.
- A formal pull request, not a draft. Exactly one label: `release:performance`. The body includes `Fixes #<this issue>`.
- Push the branch only to the operator fork. Do not push it to the upstream repository or to the GitCode mirror.
451.title: [Performance]: Register run tools once and skip unchanged per-turn prepare

## Problem
In the desktop app Model registry flow, if the **first** model connection attempt fails, fixing the model/provider settings and trying **Save & connect** again still fails. Only after **restarting ScienceDiscovery** does the same (corrected) configuration connect successfully.

## Expected

     4. Restart ScienceDiscovery; open Model registry and Save & connect with the same corrected settings.
   - **Expected result / pass criteria:** Step 3 succeeds (or fails only with a fresh, accurate error for a still-bad config). Requiring step 4 for an otherwise valid config is a fail.

## 背景

Phase2/3 合入后，旧版 `normalizeSpecialistInput` 白名单重建会**静默丢掉** `runtime`（HTTP 仍 201，看起来像创建成功但没有 Codex）。当前源码已修复：`store` 会保留并校验 `runtime`，非法则 400（`SPECIALIST_RUNTIME_INVALID`）。

日常 CI 已有 UT 覆盖（`services/api/src/specialist-runtime/runtime.test.ts` 的 create/update/reload 保留 `runtime`；`phase3.test.ts` 多 kind 保留 + 拒凭据字段）。但 **HTTP 层契约偏薄**：没有断言 `POST/PATCH /api/specialists` 响应里的 `runtime`，也没有断言非法字段 → 400。Journey 脚本能间接暴露问题，但默认不进可重复 CI。

## 目标

补上可进 CI 的 HTTP（或等价集成）用例，防止后续改动再次把 `runtime` 从 create/update 路径丢掉。

- [ ] `POST /api/specialists` 带合法 `runtime: { kind: "codex" }`（及/或 `claude-code` / `acp`）→ **2xx**，且 **响应 body 含同等 `runtime.kind`**（及已声明的非密钥元数据）。

- [ ] 用例挂在默认可重复门禁（UT/集成，**非**仅手工 journey）；失败条件明确、可本地复现。
- [ ] 不把真实密钥写进测试；不依赖外部 DeepSeek/Codex 网络。

## 非目标

- 不解决「旧 dist / 缓存包缺 `specialist-runtime`」的运维错配提示（可另开）。
- 不在本 issue 做配置页 UI / 主 Agent 代配 / Specialist CLI 卡片（见姊妹产品 issue）。

## 参考

- `services/api/src/store.ts` — `normalizeSpecialistInput` → `normalizeSpecialistRuntime`
- `services/api/src/specialist-runtime/config.ts` — `SPECIALIST_RUNTIME_INVALID`
- `services/api/src/specialist-runtime/runtime.test.ts` / `phase3.test.ts`

455.body:
## 背景

Codex/Claude Specialist（Phase2/3）体验中，配置与运维仍偏「懂进程 env + 懂 API」：

- 设置页**没有** runtime/SDK 选择器；UI 保存不发 `runtime`（只能 API 带 `runtime` 创建）。
- `SCIENCE_AGENT_CODEX_BASE_URL` **只能**写进 API 进程环境，改完需重启；主 Agent 工具 `configure_specialist_runtime` 只能改已有外部 runtime 的非密钥项，**不能**设 base URL、代填 key、引导 device-code，也不能把 native 改成 codex/cc。
- 有任务内配密卡（`CodexConfigCard` / `runtime-config`），但**没有**右侧 Specialist CLI 卡片，也**没有**「重启 specialist runtime」。

产品口径（维护者确认）：配置页保持简；复杂鉴权进主对话；保底是用户可直连 specialist，且可重启。

## 目标（三块合一，完整产品面）

### A. 配置页：选 runtime + 拉 SDK

- 配置页增加 **runtime 选择**（至少 `codex` / `claude-code` 等已支持 kind）。
- 选定后，系统下载/安装对应 SDK（失败有明确提示与可重试）。
- 表单保持简：**runtime + Skills + 描述**（名称可保留）；旁侧短文案提示：鉴权 / base URL / device-code 等在主对话由主 Agent 完成。
- 保存时 UI **必须**把所选 `runtime` 写入 create/update API（与现有 schema 对齐）。

### B. 主对话代配：加密输入 + device-code 引导

放开当前限制，主 Agent 在对话中可协助完成：

- **base URL / API key**：向用户发出**加密输入框**；用户把 key 填进输入框，**key 不进入对话正文**。
- **device-code**：主 Agent 把 code 交给用户，并说明如何在外部完成配置。
- 完成后写入平台侧安全存储 / `runtime-config` 路径，供后续委派使用（具体存储形态实现自定，验收看行为）。

### C. 右侧 Specialist 卡片 + CLI + 重启

- 会话右侧增加 **Specialist 卡片**。
- 点击后打开 **CLI 页**：展示主 Agent ↔ 该 specialist 的对话记录；用户也可在此页直接与 specialist 交互。
- 该页左侧提供 **「重启 specialist runtime」**（换 endpoint/凭证或进程异常后可重新拉起，无需整站重启 API）。

## 验收标准

- [ ] **A**：设置页可选 runtime；选定后触发 SDK 拉取；保存后 GET specialist 可见对应 `runtime.kind`；有「剩余配置在主对话完成」提示。
- [ ] **B**：主对话可走加密输入完成 base URL 与 key（正文日志/历史中不可见明文 key）；device-code 流程有用户可见引导；无需手改进程 env 即可完成常见第三方 endpoint 配置（至少覆盖当前 Codex→DeepSeek Responses 类场景的一条端到端路径）。
- [ ] **C**：右侧卡片可打开 CLI 页；可见主 Agent–specialist 记录且用户可交互；「重启 specialist runtime」可用，重启后可再次委派/交互。
- [ ] 不降低现有安全底线：Always Allow 不得代填密钥；密钥不进 specialist 元数据白名单。
- [ ] 有对应自动化或可重复手工验收步骤（可与 `test(specialist): HTTP runtime 契约` 姊妹 issue 互补，不重复）。

## 非目标

- 不在本 issue 只补 HTTP 静默丢 `runtime` 的测试（另开测试 issue）。

## 背景

原生主 Agent（`runtime-core` AgentLoop）支持一轮多个 `tool_calls`，默认可并行约 10 路（`SCIENCE_AGENT_MAX_PARALLEL_TOOL_CALLS`）。

体验后果：自由 brief（尤其 DSV 兼容端点）易报 `Codex returned an invalid platform decision`；任务被拆成多轮，延迟与首败噪音上升。

放开 specialist 路径「一轮只能一个平台工具」的硬限制，使其更接近主 Agent 的多工具能力；同时保留权限总线（原生 shell/改文件仍应走平台工具，不得悄悄打开 `shell_tool` 绕过）。

- [ ] 与 DSV 等兼容端点联调：自由 brief 的 `invalid platform decision` 首败率相对现状有可描述改进（测试或手测步骤写清）。

461.author: ink999107
461.body:
## Summary

When the runtime data directory's absolute path is 88 bytes or longer, the sandbox egress gateway cannot bind its Unix socket and **every** `run_shell` fails before any command executes — including a bare `echo`. The Runner still reports `ready: true` and `sandboxNetwork.available: true`, so the failure only appears per execution, inside the tool result, and the agent cannot tell whether the sandbox or its own command is at fault.

On Linux the limit leaves 87 bytes for the data directory; on macOS 83. A checkout whose path is already deep (for example a handoff/archive directory several levels below `$HOME`) reaches 88 bytes with the default `<repository root>/.sciencediscovery-data` and fails by exactly one byte.

## Environment

- ScienceDiscovery `54263a4c` (native local mode, `scripts/start-stack.sh --mode local --no-build --no-jiuwenswarm`), Linux, bubblewrap sandbox.
- Sandbox network access: global settings `mode: "open"` (also reproducible with `domain-allowlist`).
- Runner data directory: `SCIENCE_DISCOVERY_DATA_DIR` = `<repository root>/.sciencediscovery-data`, absolute length 88 bytes.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Place the checkout so that `<absolute repository root>/.sciencediscovery-data` is **88 bytes or longer** (equivalently, set `SCIENCE_DISCOVERY_DATA_DIR` to an 88+ byte absolute path):

   ```bash
   printf %s "$PWD/.sciencediscovery-data" | wc -c   # 88 or more → reproduces
   ```

2. Start the stack and enable sandbox network access (`open` or `domain-allowlist`) so a session's tool calls need egress.
3. In a session, run any shell command — a trivial `echo` is enough.
4. Observe: every `run_shell` fails with `status: "failed"`, empty stdout, and the same stderr, e.g.

   ```
   Sandbox network access (domain-allowlist and open) is unavailable: the egress socket path is 108 bytes,
   over this platform's 107-byte Unix socket path limit — <dataDir>/eg/<16 hex>.
   The socket has to stay inside the runner data directory, so shorten that directory by at least 1 byte(s)
   (SCIENCE_DISCOVERY_DATA_DIR); it must leave 20 bytes for the socket itself.
   ```

5. `GET /health` on the runner and the `check_runner` tool both still report `sandboxUsable: true` / `sandboxNetwork.available: true`, and `sandboxNetwork.modes` still lists `domain-allowlist` and `open`.

## Code path

- `services/runner/src/egress-gateway.ts` — `MAX_UNIX_SOCKET_PATH_BYTES` (107 Linux / 103 macOS), `EGRESS_SOCKET_RELATIVE_BYTES = 20` (`/eg/` + 16-hex digest name), `EgressGatewayRegistry.socketPath()`, and `assertUnixSocketPathFits()` called at the top of `EgressGateway.listen()`. The socket path is therefore `dataDir` length + 20, and a data directory of 88 bytes yields 108 > 107.
- `services/runner/src/executor.ts` — `prepareSandboxEgress()` calls `gateways.acquire()` on the launch path for any `domain-allowlist` / `open` execution, so the failure is charged to every execution, not only the ones that use the network.
- `services/runner/src/server.ts` — `sandboxNetworkCapability()` probes only the egress bridge's host Python interpreter. It never measures the socket path, so the capability report and `/health` claim the modes are available while every execution fails.
- `services/launcher/src/preflight.ts` / `services/runner/src/readiness.ts` — likewise check only sandbox usability (bwrap options, user namespaces), not the socket path.
- Default data directory: `.env` → `SCIENCE_DISCOVERY_DATA_DIR=.sciencediscovery-data`, resolved against the repository root in `scripts/start-stack.sh`.

## Why this is reported as a bug

- The constraint "the runtime data directory must be ≤ 87 bytes (Linux) / ≤ 83 bytes (macOS)" is real but is documented nowhere, and nothing at startup warns about it. The default layout silently depends on how deep the checkout sits.
- The failure is discovered per execution rather than at startup, and the only surface that knows the reason (`/health`, `check_runner`) reports the opposite (`available: true`). In our run the agent spent its turns proving the sandbox was broken and could not open a repair card for the blocker, so an antibody-design session ended with zero commands executed.
- Because the launch path needs the gateway for *any* command, an over-long path does not degrade network access — it takes the whole Runner offline while it still advertises itself as healthy. The preflight code already states this failure mode for bubblewrap options: reporting success from a launch the runner would refuse "is exactly the mismatch that let the service look healthy while every tool call failed".

## Suggested direction

1. Report the socket-path condition in the capability/health surface: `sandboxNetworkCapability()` (and the launcher preflight) should measure `socketPath("")` for the configured data directory and return `available: false` with the byte counts, so the blocker is visible before a session starts.
2. Fail loudly at startup: `scripts/start-stack.sh` (and the single-file launcher) should refuse to start, or warn with the exact shortfall, when the resolved data directory exceeds the platform limit.
3. Document the limit next to `SCIENCE_DISCOVERY_DATA_DIR` in `docs/{en,zh}/reference/configuration.md`, since it is a hard deployment constraint.
4. Optionally decouple the socket path from the install location — keep the digest-of-revision identity but root the socket directory in a short, runner-owned runtime path (`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`, or a 0700 directory the runner creates and verifies ownership of) so a deep checkout is not a functional constraint.

Short term, pointing `SCIENCE_DISCOVERY_DATA_DIR` at a short path (a symlink keeps the existing 2 GB of state and the absolute paths baked into `envs/` valid) unblocks the Runner.

## Impact

Total loss of code execution on an affected host for every session, with a misleading "Runner is ready" signal; no workaround is reachable from inside a session (the agent cannot change the host's data directory).
461.title: [Bug]: A deep data directory breaks the egress socket path, so every run_shell fails while the Runner reports ready

462.author: HongyeZhou
462.body:
## User request

When I switch the model in a conversation, I want the next new conversation to start with that model automatically. I should not have to select it again or separately visit settings to make that choice stick.

Example: the configured default is model A. In session 1, I explicitly select model B in the conversation model picker. Every new conversation should initially use model B rather than returning to model A: this includes another session in the same project, a session in a different project, and the first session of a newly created project, even if the target project has a different default. If I later explicitly select model C, the next new session should start with C.

## Current behavior

The conversation picker changes a session override. New sessions inherit the project default model, falling back to the system default, so a choice made in the previous conversation is not automatically reused.

This is a request to change that behavior, rather than only explain it with a tooltip.

## Expected behavior and acceptance criteria

- [ ] After an explicit, successfully saved model selection in a conversation, every new conversation starts with that selected model, across all projects and including the first session of a newly created project, without an extra confirmation or a trip to settings.
- [ ] A remembered explicit selection takes precedence over project and system model defaults when initializing any new conversation.
- [ ] A later explicit selection becomes the remembered choice for subsequent new sessions. Merely opening an older conversation does not replace the remembered choice.
- [ ] The remembered choice survives page refresh and application restart.
- [ ] Existing conversations retain their own model selection; creating a conversation does not change other conversations or an in-flight run's model.
- [ ] If there is no remembered selection, normal project-default → system-default inheritance continues to work.
- [ ] If the remembered model has been removed or is no longer selectable, creation falls back to a valid configured default, or shows actionable model configuration feedback if none exists. It must not retain a dangling model selection.
- [ ] The model shown in the new conversation matches its effective saved model. Any scope hint accurately describes the new behavior in both English and Chinese.
- [ ] Repeatable browser regression coverage verifies A → select B → create session → B within the same project, across projects with different defaults, and in a newly created project; a subsequent selection of C; persistence after reload/restart, unchanged existing conversations, and missing-model fallback.

## Selection policy

Use one last explicitly selected model for new conversations, independent of project boundaries. The user requests a Codex-style experience: choose a model once and keep using that choice when starting new conversations. This is the requested interaction policy, rather than a claim about Codex implementation details.

Project boundaries must not reset the remembered selection. Merely viewing an older conversation must not count as choosing its model. Existing conversations retain their own selection. This specifies the initialization behavior; it does not require rewriting every project's settings or changing other users' preferences. The persistence mechanism should follow the product's user/preference model.

## Related issues and current PRs

- #44 describes the same source of confusion, but its proposed solution explicitly retains session-only switching and adds a scope hint. This issue requests remembered selection for new sessions instead. Keep the two acceptance contracts distinct; a hint-only change does not satisfy this request.
- PR #289 is currently an open draft for #44. Its description explicitly says persistence/configuration/selection callbacks are unchanged. It does not implement remembered selection; its hint wording will need to be reconciled if this feature lands.
- #278 concerns configuration from within a conversation and task continuation. It does not require new sessions to reuse the last selected model.
- Closed #336 is an analogous usability request about remembering approval mode/defaults, rather than model selection.

At filing time, a search of open/closed issues and current open PRs found no exact duplicate or open PR implementing this remembered-model behavior.
462.title: [Feature]: New sessions should remember the last explicitly selected conversation model

469.author: sciencediscovery-bot[bot]
469.body:
## Correction (2026-10-22T04:2xZ)

This issue was first filed as an "intermittent CI load flake". **That was wrong.** The failure is deterministic and the root cause is a runner image change. The earlier hypothesis (concurrency/load) is withdrawn, and the "same test passes in the CI-test run" evidence was also invalid — `UT` was skipped in that run.

## What actually happens

GitHub rolled `ubuntu-latest` from **ubuntu-24.04** to **ubuntu-26.04** between 2026-10-21T10:15Z and 2026-10-22T02:22Z. The pruning path builds its "busy" set from `readlink /proc/<pid>/exe`:

```
packages/executor/src/remote-compute.ts:106
busy=$(for process in /proc/[0-9]*; do readlink "$process/exe" 2>/dev/null || true; done)
```

On ubuntu-26.04 that link no longer reports the binary a live process is executing, so the pruning pass sees an **in-use binary as stale and deletes it**. This is product code, not only a test helper: on 26.04 the same logic would delete a binary that is currently running.

## Evidence

| when (UTC) | job | runner image | `packages/executor/src/remote-compute-prune.test.ts` |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-10-21T10:16Z | `119165996742` (#467 merge group) | **ubuntu-24.04** | 2661 ms, all tests pass |
| 2026-10-22T03:31Z | `119621422198` (#468) | **ubuntu-26.04** | 3 `/bin/sh`, `/bin/dash`, `/bin/bash` cases fail |

- Runner version is `2.338.0` in both jobs; only the image changed.
- Failing run [39716847675](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/39716847675), job `119621422198`, step `Run UT`: planned 4441 / executed 4441 / passed 4438 / **failed 3** / skipped 0.
- Failure artifact `ut/tagged/group-141/worker-1-events.jsonl`: actual has an extra `'b' x 64` — the busy binary was pruned. The other 4 tests in the file pass.
- `merge-gate` (job `119626303432`) only aggregates: `CI gate failed: ut: failure`.
- Every PR after the switch shows the same signature: #269 #316 #460 #463 #465 #466 #467 #468.

## Impact

`UT` is a required check, so **no PR can enter the merge queue** for reasons unrelated to its own diff — the pipeline is blocked repo-wide.

## Suggested fix

1. Short term (unblocks the queue): pin the UT job to `ubuntu-24.04` (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:194` uses `runs-on: ubuntu-latest`).
2. Correct fix: stop deriving "busy" from `readlink /proc/<pid>/exe` alone. Compare device+inode via `stat -L /proc/<pid>/exe` against the file being pruned (works when the link target is not readable), and log the observed `busy` set when a removal is skipped, so the next platform change is diagnosable from CI logs.
3. Add a regression test that fails if a running binary is pruned — the existing test is the right shape, but it needs to run on the platforms we actually support.
469.title: bug(executor): pruning treats live binaries as stale on ubuntu-26.04 runners (busy detection uses readlink /proc/<pid>/exe)
